summary.title: Sega Master System Emulator: Memory Map and Paging
summary.one_liner: You learn how the Sega Master System address space, ROM/RAM bank mapping registers, and Codemasters mapper work, and how to structure Z80 memory read and write routines in an emulator.
keywords: how to emulate sega master system paging
takeaways: The SMS address space is split into three 16 KB ROM slots, an optional RAM bank in slot 3, and 8 KB of mirrored work RAM.
Writes to the 0xFFFC-0xFFFF registers select ROM pages for each slot and control which of two RAM banks is mapped into slot 3.
The Codemasters mapper uses writes to 0x0, 0x4000 and 0x8000 instead, and has no RAM banking.
Storing a page index per slot and looking up cartridge data on read avoids slow memcpy on every bank switch.
All memory writes should go through one function so ROM protection, mirroring and paging can be handled in one place.
summary.summary: The page is a written tutorial by the author of a Sega Master System emulator, describing the SMS memory map and how the memory mapper registers at 0xFFFC-0xFFFF page ROM and RAM banks. It explains the Codemasters variant, then walks through C++ WriteMemory, DoMemPage, DoMemPageCM and ReadMemory functions. The author stores a current page number per slot and reads cartridge data directly instead of copying pages, which the author notes is to avoid slow memcpy calls.
